context_documents.title: 2024-4613 · Different contact stiffness enables amp delivery without a pivot
context_documents.body:
# 2024-4613: Different contact stiffness enables amp delivery without a pivot

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

The under-bumper collector and guides feed two independently driven launcher rollers. The interview describes a lower-durometer lower contact relative to the upper contact, combined with speed control, to curve the amp delivery without moving the whole launcher. A deflector protects the climber from dropped notes.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly chose the contact/speed arrangement to perform both speaker and amp tasks without a pivot, with robustness as a stated benefit. The climber guard responds to the possibility of a falling note disabling it.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Eliminating an angle actuator shifts trajectory control into contact deformation, spin and launch speed. That reduces joints and moving wiring, but may increase sensitivity to note wear, temperature and compression. The guard illustrates that a rare dropped piece can create a structural failure state even when the main transport path works.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Map amp accuracy with used notes, varying voltage and repeated shooting. Test the dropped-note guard from several directions and verify that it does not obstruct normal climbing.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

source_reviews.title: Barker Redbacks robot reveal and Q&A
facts: The billet chassis took approximately five machining hours. The team describes close-fitting bumper brackets, slotted subsystem attachments and collision robustness as design goals.
source_reviews.limitations: Team claims do not quantify collision forces or prove durability limits. Forum alloy references are ambiguous.

source_reviews.title: Barker Redbacks reveal Q&A
facts: Upper and lower wheels use different hardness. The team tied amp consistency to the condition of the note and to driver practice.
source_reviews.limitations: No percentages, durometers or launch calibration given. Other replies about dimensions and module repackaging are community comments.

source_reviews.title: Barker Redbacks Behind the Bumpers
facts: Older dossier describes a fixed launcher angle, beam-break staging and a spring-deployed single hook.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: The Barker Redbacks paired a compact billet base with a scorer whose frame angle stays fixed in the inherited account. The team says the rigid, accurately located chassis interfaces were intended to preserve the robot's condition through fast contact. For amp, the team explicitly points to upper/lower wheel hardness and practiced driving, with degraded notes as a boundary. The chassis and launch strategy are linked because a fixed exit geometry leaves the driver and controls to set shot position and heading consistently.
piece_flow: An inset floor pickup and low-friction guides deliver the note in the older study.
Beam-break staging establishes when the note can be fed into the fixed wheel pair.
Speaker and amp use different operating conditions for the same release. The team reply establishes unequal wheel hardness but does not supply the actual relative speeds.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: A low compact frame restricts the intake opening and the room for swerve hardware. Use the chassis slots as inspection datums and separate the envelope of the note from the structure carrying impact loads. Fixed shooting eliminates a pivot sweep, but the placement task reappears as a constraint on chassis alignment and on how the note leaves the wheels.

subsystems.name: Billet chassis
subsystems.construction: Machined billet chassis with close-fitting bumper brackets and slots for subsystem interfaces.
subsystems.operation: Carry drive and impact loads while locating attached mechanisms.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team wanted stable interfaces and fewer collision-related changes over an event.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Accurately machined datums reduce assembly stack-up. A monolithic structure can still transmit a hit to a module, shaft or bracket, and field replacement can be costly if damage reaches the main member.
subsystems.interfaces: Slot geometry, bumper support and access for module extraction.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Measure alignment after repeated representative impacts and verify replacement time at the module and bracket level.
subsystems.unknowns: Material temper, machining setup time beyond stated cutting time and load measurements.

subsystems.name: Fixed launcher and feed
subsystems.construction: Inherited fixed-angle launcher, protected feed and staging sensors. Team confirms different top and bottom wheel hardness.
subsystems.operation: Feed the note after staging and establish a launch appropriate for the target from a chosen chassis position.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team reports satisfactory amp performance with notes in usable condition and drivers who practiced.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Unequal compliance can shift effective compression, traction and exit rotation. Degraded notes may interact differently with the two contact surfaces, so a single calibration on new notes can overstate robustness.
subsystems.interfaces: Intake alignment, note condition, wheel recovery and chassis positioning enter the same shot outcome.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Proposed checks include repeat shots at deliberate pose offsets with intact and worn notes, plus wheel replacement repeatability.
subsystems.unknowns: Actual wheel specifications, setpoints and verified accuracy distribution.

subsystems.name: Compact chain hook
subsystems.construction: Older dossier describes a spring-extended telescopic hook pulled by a winch and shielded against stray notes.
subsystems.operation: Reach the chain and pull the chassis into a hanging state.
subsystems.team_rationale: The inherited study attributes the cover to keeping fallen notes out of the hook area.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A cover should block loose notes while preserving inspection and safe access to a loaded mechanism.
subsystems.interfaces: Hook travel and chain approach have to clear chassis and scorer.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test deployment after a note falls into the surrounding package. Inspect line routing and return behavior after a partial catch.
subsystems.unknowns: Hook construction drawings and installed event changes.

revisions: The revealed chassis and wheel pairing were confirmed in team replies. Later changes are unresolved.
transferable_principles: Treat fixed-angle shooting as a system requirement for pose control and note condition. Use machined datums where their post-impact repeatability justifies the fabrication cost.
disconfirming_conditions: A fixed trajectory loses value if good shots require approaching through congested locations or the amp window is too sensitive to note damage. Billet has limited value if critical impact failures occur in attached parts.
remaining_gaps: Code behavior, full caption review, drivetrain drawing and empirical speaker/amp shot envelope.
recommended_images: Side view of upper/lower wheel contact with note present
